partner_context.their_ambition: Fullers360 is Auckland's primary ferry operator, carrying commuters and visitors across the Waitematā Harbour and the Hauraki Gulf — to Devonport, Waiheke, Rangitoto and beyond — and has committed to decarbonizing its fleet toward Auckland's zero-emission transport goals.
partner_context.their_pressure: Auckland Transport and the Council have set hard low-emission ferry targets; the existing diesel fleet is ageing, the Waiheke commuter run is busy and weather-exposed, and conventional electric ferries are slow and range-limited across the Gulf's longer legs.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: Navier delivers vessels that are zero-emission AND faster AND smoother across the Gulf chop — taking the high-frequency Waiheke and Devonport commuter legs, satisfying the decarbonization mandate, and opening longer Gulf island links the diesel fleet runs slowly today.

hero.title: Navier × Fullers360 — the Hauraki Gulf, flying and clean
hero.subtitle: Foiling-electric vessels for Auckland's zero-emission ferry future.
hero.what_we_do_together: Navier brings a software-defined foiling-electric fleet that meets Auckland's low-emission ferry mandate while flying faster and quieter than the diesel ferries it replaces. Fullers360 brings the wharves, the Hauraki Gulf network and the commuter demand — together modernizing one of the southern hemisphere's great ferry operations.

why_now: Auckland Transport has committed to a low-emission ferry future and Fullers360 is decarbonizing its fleet. The Waiheke and Devonport commuter runs are busy and growing; the Gulf's longer island legs are slow on diesel. A tier that is clean AND faster is exactly what the mandate and the commuter need now.
multimodal_fit: Navier slots into the existing Fullers360 network from downtown Auckland's ferry terminal — Devonport, Waiheke, Rangitoto, Half Moon Bay — taking high-frequency commuter legs integrated with AT HOP ticketing, while conventional ferries keep the heaviest vehicle and trunk routes.

differentiation.why_navier: The only foiling-electric platform that meets Auckland's low-emission ferry mandate while being faster and quieter than the diesel fleet — software-defined, autonomy-ready, integrable with AT HOP ticketing and existing wharves.

proof_points.detail: Auckland Transport has set low-emission ferry targets; Fullers360 is decarbonizing its fleet.

proof_points.claim: Ferry demand is large and growing.
proof_points.detail: Fullers360 carries millions of trips a year across the Waitematā Harbour and Hauraki Gulf.
AT HOP spans ferries, buses and trains — a ready multimodal backbone.

proof_points.claim: The platform is proven in service.
proof_points.detail: 10 vessels delivered, 4,000+ flight hours, 2025 production sold out.

objections.response: The foil flies above the chop for a smoother ride than a diesel ferry on the Waiheke run. Pioneer II covers the harbour and inner-Gulf commuter legs all-electric; Quanta-LR carries the longer Northland and Coromandel runs.
objections.concern: Can it handle the Gulf chop?

objections.response: Yes — it runs from existing Fullers360 wharves and integrates with AT HOP ticketing; only a berth pedestal for charging is needed, no new terminal.
objections.concern: Does it integrate with AT HOP and the wharves?

objections.response: Phased like any fleet renewal — start on the busy Waiheke or Devonport corridor, prove the economics and reliability, then scale as diesel vessels retire.
objections.concern: Is it a fit for a ferry operator's economics?

objections.response: Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal at key wharves; the harbour and inner-Gulf legs sit well inside the all-electric range with charging at terminus wharves between runs.
objections.concern: What about charging across the Gulf?

the_ask.navier_brings: The software-defined foiling-electric fleet, captain training, certification path and the operating playbook for harbour and island ferry service.
the_ask.partner_brings: Wharf access, AT HOP integration, the route-by-route rollout sequence and the ferry-operations pathway.
the_ask.next_step: Launch a Waiheke or Devonport pilot corridor in 2027 and scale across the Gulf as the diesel fleet retires.

close.title: The Gulf, finally flying.
close.body: Auckland already committed to zero-emission ferries. Navier is the tier that makes clean also mean faster and smoother — modernizing one of the southern hemisphere's great ferry operations while meeting the mandate.

why_navier_now.step_change: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water, so a Navier vessel flies instead of plowing through chop - roughly 10x more efficient than a conventional planing boat, faster (30+ kt cruise), and dramatically smoother and quieter. It's software-defined and autonomy-ready, so the same fleet keeps getting better and cheaper to run over time.
why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: Navier rides on infrastructure that already exists - the open water and the berths and jetties already in use. No vertiports, no new rights-of-way. Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal; the Quanta-LR hybrid needs no charging infrastructure at all.
why_navier_now.the_moment: Three forces just converged: the technology crossed from prototype to platform (10 vessels delivered, 4,000+ flight hours, 2025 production sold out), decarbonization mandates turned legacy diesel fleets into stranded liabilities, and the hybrid removed the 'no charging' excuse. The marine layer is being claimed cluster-by-cluster right now.

revenue_potential.anchor_note: $4.7M/yr premium sea-transfer spend on sourced corridors today — the anchor every rung builds from.

whose_money_legend.navier_transport_revenue: Fare the Navier boats collect. This is the corridor P&L (atom.py). SOM/SAM rungs are in this unit.
whose_money_legend.journey_gmv: Total guest journey spend across transport, food, stays, experiences, and ancillary revenue the partner monetizes on-island. Journey GMV rung is in this unit.

revenue_potential.cite_rule: Cite MID. 'High' stacks every optimistic assumption — ceiling, not headline.

ladder_transitions.headline: Same 10% capture, expanded to the full mapped network
ladder_transitions.basis: Width-only step. Capture rate held at 10%; corridor set expands from sourced flagships to the full mapped network.

ladder_transitions.headline: Network matures: faster, more comfortable boats grow the market + leading-operator capture
ladder_transitions.basis: Two-lever step. (1) Faster, more comfortable boats grow the cross-water market (induced demand). (2) Leading-operator capture lifts share from 10% floor to 25% mature, network-wide.

ladder_transitions.headline: Lens shift: Navier captured share → total inducible marine-transfer wallet
ladder_transitions.basis: Unit change. Divide SAM (the captured share) by leading-operator capture rate to recover the full inducible water-transfer market — the marine-mobility TAM.

ladder_transitions.headline: Marine transfer → total journey wallet (food, stays, experiences, in-app ads)
ladder_transitions.basis: Journey-wallet step. Each $1 of marine-transfer spend unlocks ~$3 of broader journey GMV across merchants the partner monetizes.
